from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Big Question: Why Sum Variables?", [
            "We often combine independent random processes.",
            "Let Z be the sum of X and Y.",
            "Total delivery time equals travel plus unloading time."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display formula Z = X + Y in #FFFFFF at center of grid.
        formula = MathTex("Z = X + Y", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            Write(formula)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Character 'Delivery Robot' appears in #ADD8E6 
        # with 'Travel Time' (X) and 'Unloading Time' (Y) labels.
        
        # Robot representation (Vectorized group)
        robot_color = "#ADD8E6"
        body = Square(side_length=0.6, color=robot_color, fill_opacity=1)
        head = Square(side_length=0.3, color=robot_color, fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.45)
        eye_l = Dot(head.get_center() + LEFT*0.07 + UP*0.05, radius=0.03, color=BLACK)
        eye_r = Dot(head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.07 + UP*0.05, radius=0.03, color=BLACK)
        robot = VGroup(body, head, eye_l, eye_r)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Component X (Travel Time)
        bar_x = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.3, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
        label_x = MathTex("X", color="#FFFF00").scale(0.8).next_to(bar_x, UP, buff=0.1)
        x_comp = VGroup(bar_x, label_x)
        self.place_at_grid(x_comp, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Component Y (Unloading Time)
        bar_y = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.3, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
        label_y = MathTex("Y", color="#00FF00").scale(0.8).next_to(bar_y, UP, buff=0.1)
        y_comp = VGroup(bar_y, label_y)
        self.place_at_grid(y_comp, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            FadeIn(robot),
            FadeIn(x_comp),
            FadeIn(y_comp)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Z as the total span with a bracket in #FF69B4.
        
        # Combined bars to show total span
        bar_x_copy = bar_x.copy()
        bar_y_copy = bar_y.copy()
        combined_bars = VGroup(bar_x_copy, bar_y_copy).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(combined_bars, "F3", "F4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        bracket = Brace(combined_bars, direction=DOWN, color="#FF69B4")
        z_label = MathTex("Z = X + Y", color="#FF69B4").scale(0.8).next_to(bracket, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            TransformFromCopy(VGroup(bar_x, bar_y), combined_bars),
            Create(bracket),
            FadeIn(z_label)
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "Prerequisite: The Discrete Logic"
        lecture_lines = [
            "For independent variables, the joint probability is their product.",
            "To find the sum's probability, sum all valid pairs.",
            "On a grid, these pairs form a diagonal line."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show grid with axes labeled X and Y in #FFFFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        grid_dots = VGroup()
        for r in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]:
            for c in ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]:
                dot = Dot(color=GRAY, radius=0.06)
                self.place_at_grid(dot, f"{r}{c}")
                grid_dots.add(dot)
                
        # Label axes X and Y
        x_axis_label = Text("X (Die 1)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        y_axis_label = Text("Y (Die 2)", font_size=20, color=WHITE).rotate(90 * DEGREES)
        
        # Position using grid constraints
        self.place_in_area(x_axis_label, "F1", "F6")
        x_axis_label.shift(DOWN * 0.8)
        
        self.place_in_area(y_axis_label, "A1", "F1")
        y_axis_label.shift(LEFT * 0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Create(grid_dots),
            Write(x_axis_label),
            Write(y_axis_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight points (1,3), (2,2), (3,1) in #FFFF00 on the grid.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Mapping: (Die1=x, Die2=y)
        # Die1 = Col 1, 2, 3...
        # Die2 = Row F (1), E (2), D (3), C (4), B (5), A (6)
        # (1,3) -> D1
        # (2,2) -> E2
        # (3,1) -> F3
        target_cells = ["D1", "E2", "F3"]
        highlights = VGroup()
        coord_labels = VGroup()
        
        for pos in target_cells:
            h_dot = Dot(color="#FFFF00", radius=0.12)
            self.place_at_grid(h_dot, pos)
            highlights.add(h_dot)
            
            # Label
            label_text = "(1,3)" if pos == "D1" else "(2,2)" if pos == "E2" else "(3,1)"
            label = Text(label_text, font_size=16, color="#FFFF00")
            self.place_at_grid(label, pos)
            label.next_to(h_dot, UR, buff=0.05)
            coord_labels.add(label)
            
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[Flash(h, color="#FFFF00") for h in highlights], lag_ratio=0.3),
            FadeIn(highlights),
            Write(coord_labels),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a diagonal line through these points in #FF00FF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Diagonal line covering the highlighted points
        diag_line = Line(
            start=self.grid["D1"],
            end=self.grid["F3"],
            color="#FF00FF",
            stroke_width=6
        )
        # Extend slightly to show it's a line x+y=4
        diag_line.scale(1.4)
        
        self.play(Create(diag_line), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final cleanup for color consistency
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "For continuous variables, we transition from sums to integrals.",
            "The probability density of the sum is the convolution.",
            "The formula integrates the product of the two densities.",
            "The term z minus x is the remaining value.",
            "This calculates the probability density at any point z."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Continuous Leap: The Convolution Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # For continuous variables, we transition from sums to integrals.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        sum_sym = MathTex(r"\sum", font_size=80, color=YELLOW)
        int_sym = MathTex(r"\int", font_size=80, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_sym, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_sym))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            Transform(sum_sym, int_sym),
            Flash(self.grid["A3"], color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.5)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The probability density of the sum is the convolution.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"f_Z(z) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f_X(x) f_Y(z-x) dx",
            font_size=40,
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "C6")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The formula integrates the product of the two densities.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Axes for PDF curves
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 24},
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "D1", "F6")
        
        # Define two PDFs
        # f_X is centered at 0
        def pdf_x(x): return np.exp(-x**2)
        # f_Y(z-x) is centered at x=z. Let's pick z=1.5
        def pdf_y_shifted(x): return 0.8 * np.exp(-(x-1.5)**2)
        
        curve_x = axes.plot(pdf_x, color="#ADD8E6")
        curve_y = axes.plot(pdf_y_shifted, color="#90EE90")
        
        label_x = MathTex("f_X(x)", color="#ADD8E6", font_size=24)
        label_y = MathTex("f_Y(z-x)", color="#90EE90", font_size=24)
        
        # Manual positioning near curves relative to axes
        label_x.move_to(axes.c2p(-1.5, 0.8))
        label_y.move_to(axes.c2p(2.5, 0.6))

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve_x), Create(curve_y))
        self.play(FadeIn(label_x), FadeIn(label_y))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The term z minus x is the remaining value.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Mark point x on f_X and z-x on f_Y
        x_val = 0.5
        
        # Corrected method: input_to_graph_point instead of i2p
        line_x = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.input_to_graph_point(x_val, curve_x), color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        dot_x = Dot(axes.input_to_graph_point(x_val, curve_x), color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        line_y = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.input_to_graph_point(x_val, curve_y), color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        dot_y = Dot(axes.input_to_graph_point(x_val, curve_y), color=WHITE, radius=0.06)

        label_coord = MathTex("x", color=WHITE, font_size=24).next_to(axes.c2p(x_val, 0), DOWN)

        self.play(Create(line_x), FadeIn(dot_x))
        self.play(Create(line_y), FadeIn(dot_y))
        self.play(FadeIn(label_coord))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This calculates the probability density at any point z.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight product by shading overlap area in YELLOW
        def pdf_prod(x): return pdf_x(x) * pdf_y_shifted(x)
        curve_prod = axes.plot(pdf_prod, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        area_prod = axes.get_area(curve_prod, color=YELLOW, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(Create(curve_prod))
        self.play(FadeIn(area_prod))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing Convolution: Flip and Slide"
        lecture_lines = [
            "First, we flip the second distribution's graph horizontally.",
            "Then, we slide it along the x-axis by distance z.",
            "At each position, multiply the two overlapping functions.",
            "The area under this product is the resulting density.",
            "Uniform distributions convolve into a triangular shape."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_X = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_Y = "#90EE90"
        COLOR_OVERLAP = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_RESULT = "#FF69B4"
        COLOR_FLASH = "#FFFFFF"

        # 1. Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.5, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20, "color": GREY_C}
        ).add_coordinates()
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        x_label = axes.get_x_axis_label("t").scale(0.7)
        y_label = axes.get_y_axis_label("f(t)").scale(0.7)

        # f_X(t) - fixed square wave (Uniform[0,1])
        fx_points = [axes.c2p(-1.5, 0), axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 1), axes.c2p(1, 1), axes.c2p(1, 0), axes.c2p(2.5, 0)]
        fx_graph = VMobject(color=COLOR_X, stroke_width=4).set_points_as_corners(fx_points)
        fx_text = MathTex("f_X(t)", color=COLOR_X, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(fx_text, "B3")

        # f_Y(t) - initial state (Uniform[0,1])
        fy_init_points = [axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 1), axes.c2p(1, 1), axes.c2p(1, 0)]
        fy_graph = VMobject(color=COLOR_Y, stroke_width=4).set_points_as_corners(fy_init_points)
        fy_text = MathTex("f_Y(t)", color=COLOR_Y, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(fy_text, "B5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # First, we flip the second distribution's graph horizontally.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_Y)
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(fx_graph), Write(fx_text))
        self.play(Create(fy_graph), Write(fy_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # Flipping f_Y: (t) -> (-t) which moves the pulse from [0,1] to [-1, 0]
        fy_flipped_points = [axes.c2p(-1.5, 0), axes.c2p(-1, 0), axes.c2p(-1, 1), axes.c2p(0, 1), axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(2.5, 0)]
        fy_flipped_text = MathTex("f_Y(-t)", color=COLOR_Y, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(fy_flipped_text, "B1")

        self.play(
            fy_graph.animate.set_points_as_corners(fy_flipped_points),
            Transform(fy_text, fy_flipped_text)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Then, we slide it along the x-axis by distance z.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_Y)
        
        z_tracker = ValueTracker(0.0) 
        
        def update_fy_sliding(mob):
            z = z_tracker.get_value()
            pts = [axes.c2p(-1.5, 0), axes.c2p(z-1, 0), axes.c2p(z-1, 1), axes.c2p(z, 1), axes.c2p(z, 0), axes.c2p(2.5, 0)]
            mob.set_points_as_corners(pts)

        fy_graph.add_updater(update_fy_sliding)
        
        fy_label_moving = MathTex("f_Y(z-t)", color=COLOR_Y, font_size=24)
        def update_fy_label(mob):
            z = z_tracker.get_value()
            mob.move_to(axes.c2p(z-0.5, 1.3, 0))
        
        fy_label_moving.add_updater(update_fy_label)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(fy_text),
            FadeIn(fy_label_moving),
            z_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2), 
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # At each position, multiply the two overlapping functions.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_OVERLAP)
        
        overlap_poly = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(0,0), axes.c2p(0,1), axes.c2p(0,1), axes.c2p(0,0),
            fill_color=COLOR_OVERLAP, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0
        )
        
        def update_overlap(mob):
            z = z_tracker.get_value()
            start = max(0, z-1)
            end = min(1, z)
            if start < end:
                mob.set_points_as_corners([
                    axes.c2p(start, 0),
                    axes.c2p(start, 1),
                    axes.c2p(end, 1),
                    axes.c2p(end, 0)
                ])
                mob.set_fill(opacity=0.5)
            else:
                mob.set_fill(opacity=0)

        overlap_poly.add_updater(update_overlap)
        self.add(overlap_poly)
        
        self.play(z_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The area under this product is the resulting density.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_RESULT)
        
        result_curve = VMobject(color=COLOR_RESULT, stroke_width=5)
        result_curve.set_points_as_corners([axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 0)])

        def update_result(mob):
            z = z_tracker.get_value()
            steps = np.linspace(0, z, 50)
            pts = []
            for s in steps:
                val = 0
                if 0 <= s <= 1: val = s
                elif 1 < s <= 2: val = 2 - s
                elif s > 2: val = 0
                pts.append(axes.c2p(s, val))
            mob.set_points_as_corners(pts)
            
        result_curve.add_updater(update_result)
        self.add(result_curve)

        self.play(z_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Uniform distributions convolve into a triangular shape.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_RESULT)
        
        flash = Flash(axes.c2p(1, 1), color=COLOR_FLASH, flash_radius=0.4, line_length=0.2)
        self.play(flash)
        
        self.play(z_tracker.animate.set_value(2.2), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Key Properties & The Central Limit Theorem Hint"
        lines = [
            "Convolution generally smooths out the resulting distribution.",
            "The sum of two uniform variables becomes triangular.",
            "Convolving again makes the distribution even smoother.",
            "Repeated convolution leads towards a bell-shaped curve.",
            "This illustrates the famous Central Limit Theorem."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # --- Persistent Objects ---
        # Right side axes for plotting distributions
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 18, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6")
        self.add(axes)

        # 1. Square Wave (Uniform on [-0.5, 0.5])
        square_curve = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 1.0 if abs(x) <= 0.5 else 0.0,
            discontinuities=[-0.5, 0.5],
            dt=0.01,
            color=WHITE
        )

        # 2. Triangle Wave (n=2, sum of two uniforms on [-1, 1])
        triangle_curve = axes.plot(
            lambda x: max(0, 1 - abs(x)),
            color="#ADD8E6",
            use_smoothing=False
        )

        # 3. Irwin-Hall (n=3, centered on [-1.5, 1.5])
        def n3_pdf(x):
            xp = x + 1.5
            if 0 <= xp < 1:
                return 0.5 * xp**2
            elif 1 <= xp < 2:
                return 0.5 * (-2 * (xp-1)**2 + 2*(xp-1) + 1)
            elif 2 <= xp <= 3:
                return 0.5 * (3-xp)**2
            return 0

        n3_curve = axes.plot(
            n3_pdf,
            color="#ADD8E6"
        )

        # 4. Normal Distribution (Gaussian)
        def gaussian_pdf(x):
            # Variance for sum of n uniforms U(-0.5, 0.5) is n/12. For n=4, sigma = sqrt(4/12) approx 0.57.
            # We use sigma=0.7 for better visualization on axes.
            sigma = 0.7 
            return (1 / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * (x / sigma)**2)

        gaussian_curve = axes.plot(
            gaussian_pdf,
            color="#FFFF00"
        )
        
        normal_label = Text("Normal Distribution", font_size=22, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(normal_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # 5. Central Limit Theorem Label
        clt_label = Text("Central Limit Theorem", font_size=28, color="#FF69B4")
        self.place_at_grid(clt_label, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Convolution generally smooths out the resulting distribution.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(square_curve), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The sum of two uniform variables becomes triangular.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.play(Transform(square_curve, triangle_curve), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Convolving again makes the distribution even smoother.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.play(Transform(square_curve, n3_curve), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Repeated convolution leads towards a bell-shaped curve.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(
            Transform(square_curve, gaussian_curve),
            Write(normal_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This illustrates the famous Central Limit Theorem.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF69B4")
        self.play(
            FadeIn(clt_label, shift=UP),
            Indicate(clt_label, color="#FF69B4"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines

        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Remember the process: identify, flip-and-slide, and integrate.
        # Combine their PDF curves using the 'Flip and Slide' motion.
        
        pdf_turtle = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=1.2, color="#90EE90", fill_opacity=0.4)
        pdf_hare = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=1.2, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.4)
        
        pdf_t_label = MathTex("f_X(x)", font_size=24, color="#90EE90")
        pdf_h_label = MathTex("f_Y(y)", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        
        pdf_t_group = VGroup(pdf_turtle, pdf_t_label.next_to(pdf_turtle, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.play(
            pdf_h_group.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]),

        )

        self.play(FadeIn(res_group))
        self.play(Flash(res_pdf, color=WHITE, flash_radius=1.2))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Sum of Independent Random Variables & The Convolution Formula
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM or Introductory Probability

sections.title: The Big Question: Why Sum Variables?
sections.content: Introduce the scenario where the outcome is the result of two independent random processes. Define Z = X + Y. Visually, show a character 'Delivery Robot' whose total delivery time (Z) is the sum of 'Travel Time' (X) and 'Unloading Time' (Y).
sections.example: If the Travel Time is roughly 10 mins and Unloading is 5 mins, what is the probability the robot takes exactly 15 mins? It’s not just one possibility; it could be 9+6, 11+4, etc.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Discrete Logic
sections.content: Before the calculus, understand the logic using a discrete grid. If X and Y are independent, the joint probability is the product. To find P(X+Y=z), we sum all combinations of (x, y) such that y = z - x.
sections.example: Rolling two dice: To get a sum of 4, we look at the diagonal of a grid: (1,3), (2,2), and (3,1). Animation shows these points lighting up on a 2D coordinate plane.

sections.title: The Continuous Leap: The Convolution Formula
sections.content: Transition from summation (Σ) to integration (∫). Introduce the PDF formula for Z: f_Z(z) = ∫ f_X(x) * f_Y(z - x) dx. Explain that 'z-x' is the mathematical way of saying 'whatever is left over for Y after X is chosen'.
sections.example: Graphically show two probability density curves (PDFs). Highlight a point 'x' on the first curve and its corresponding 'z-x' on the second.

sections.title: Visualizing Convolution: Flip and Slide
sections.content: This is the core visual concept. To compute the integral, we: 1. Flip the graph of f_Y (mirroring it). 2. Slide it along the x-axis by 'z' units. 3. Calculate the area of the overlap. The area of overlap at each position 'z' is the value of the new PDF.
sections.example: Imagine two rectangular pulses (uniform distributions) approaching each other. As they overlap, the resulting PDF grows into a triangle and then shrinks—this shows why the sum of two uniform variables is a triangular distribution.

sections.title: Key Properties & The Central Limit Theorem Hint
sections.content: Explain that convolution usually 'smooths' the distribution. Mention that if we keep adding more variables, the shape eventually becomes a Bell Curve (Normal Distribution).
sections.example: An animation showing a square wave convolving with itself multiple times, morphing from a square to a triangle, then gradually into a smooth Gaussian bell curve.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Check
sections.content: Recap the 3-step process: Identify independence, apply the 'Flip and Slide' convolution, and calculate the resulting area. Emphasize that this is how engineers calculate noise interference or total project durations.
sections.example: A 'Turtle' and a 'Hare' both finish tasks with random durations. The convolution of their time PDFs tells us the total probability of when they will both be finished.
